It is possible to grief attack on settling an PUT Option.

## Proof of Concept
If an PUT Option is In-The-Money, it will be [settled](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L315-L369) and collateral token will be transferred from perpetual vault LP to rdpx rdpxV2Core:
```
    collateralToken.safeTransferFrom(
      addresses.perpetualAtlanticVaultLP,
      addresses.rdpxV2Core,
      ethAmount
    );
```
After that, it will update collateral token balance of perpetual vault LP:
```
    IPerpetualAtlanticVaultLP(addresses.perpetualAtlanticVaultLP).subtractLoss(
      ethAmount
    );
```
It is worth noting that [subtractLoss](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#L199-L205) will check if enough collateral was sent out and it requires the collateral token balance of perpetual vault LP is equal to the `_totalCollateral - loss`:
```
  function subtractLoss(uint256 loss) public onlyPerpVault {
    require(
      collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) == _totalCollateral - loss,
      "Not enough collateral was sent out"
    );
    _totalCollateral -= loss;
  }
```
It is possible that an attacker grief attack on settling by sending some amount of collateral token to perpetual vault LP, then the require statement above will fail and settling transaction will revert.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
The culprit is that `_totalCollateral` is not synced before settling, it is recommended to do so to ensure settling transaction cannot be grief attacked. 


## Assessed type

DoS

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L975-L990

# Vulnerability details



## Description
This issue occurs as the `totalWethDelegated` variable is not updated when the user withdraws unused delegated collateral. As this variable is not updated, the sync() function may revert if the current contract's balance of Weth is lesser than the `totalWethDelegated` var. 

An attacker can easily influence the number in this variable by delegating his collateral and withdrawing repeatedly.

This situation is a problem as the sync() variable is called when `reLP` is active, so the whole bonding mechanism (functionality) will revert, and reLP will not be possible.

## Impact
Denial of service of whole Bonding mechanism in Core contract when reLP is active. And also the DoS of reLP.


## Proof of Concept
### Attack scenario
- IsreLP is set to True;
1. The attacker delegates a large amount of collateral (WETH). The totalWethDelegated variable is increased.
2. The attacker immediately withdraws his collateral before it is used.
3. The totalWethDelegated variable is not decreased due to missing updates at the withdraw function.
   - *Note: The attacker can do steps 1 and 2 repeatedly, as also on Arbitrum, the gas is cheap.*
4. Now, the User Alice wants to Bond. But this will revert as reLP is active, and in this function, a sync() is called, which will revert due to underflow.

### Missing update
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L975-L990

issues.title: Relp asset token reserve sync mechanism may cause protocol dos
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/reLP/ReLPContract.sol#L202-L307


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
 
Protocol will relp asset token reserve when user bond with delegate bonding way every time. But when protocol reLP, it use UniswapV2Library#getReserves function to get the tokens reserve, that's the problem because the uniswap pool reserves can get controlled by attacker. So attacker can use flashloan to control the uniswap pool reserves, then protocol will relp with the wrong token reserves and sync reserveAsset's balance. After that, some functions depend the `reserveAsset` parameter maybe abnormal. For example, when admin call the `lowerDepeg` function, protocol will decrease `RDPX` and `WETH` token balance, if `reserveAsset[reservesIndex["RDPX"]].tokenBalance` become very small, the protocol `RdpxV2Core#lowerDepeg` function will revert.


## Proof of Concept

1. Attacker flashloan many WETH from floshloan provider, swap WETH to RDPX to decrease the RDPX reserve to 2 ether. 
2. Attacker call `RdpxV2Core#bondWithDelegate` to sync the `reserveAsset` parameter.
3. Attacker swap back to WETH and repay flashloan.
4. When dpxETH depeg, admin call `RdpxV2Core#lowerDepeg` function will revert directly when `_rdpxAmount` is greater than 2 ether because such code: `reserveAsset[reservesIndex["RDPX"]].tokenBalance -= _rdpxAmount`.

## Tools Used

vscode, manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Protocol should use uniswap TWAP mechanism to sync the asset tokens's balance.

Uniswap

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

Inconsistent accounting for the burned and fee portions of the rDPX:

    Burned Amount: Calculated as `(_rdpxAmount * rdpxBurnPercentage) / 1e10`.
    Fee Amount: Calculated as `(_rdpxAmount * rdpxFeePercentage) / 1e10`.

In RdpxV2Core.sol within `_transfer`, when a user bonds w/ rDPX directly:

```

      IERC20WithBurn(reserveAsset[reservesIndex["RDPX"]].tokenAddress).burn(
        (_rdpxAmount * rdpxBurnPercentage) / 1e10
      );


      // transfer the rdpx to the fee distributor
      IERC20WithBurn(reserveAsset[reservesIndex["RDPX"]].tokenAddress)
        .safeTransfer(
          addresses.feeDistributor,
          (_rdpxAmount * rdpxFeePercentage) / 1e10
        );
```

These amounts are not subtracted from the internal token balance increase, leading to an inflated balance in `reserveAsset[reservesIndex["RDPX"]].tokenBalance`, directly compromising user and protocol funds.

When` _bondId == 0 `(No Existing Bond)

5. Calculates an extra amount of rDPX to withdraw.
6. Withdraws the total rDPX (including the extra amount) from the reserve.
7. Increases the token balance of the reserve asset by the entire withdrawn amount.

issues.title: Vulnerability in the withdraw function that could allow a delegate to withdraw more ETH than they should be able to
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L983
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L985


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Delegates could slowly drain additional ETH over multiple withdraws

## Proof of Concept
There is a potential vulnerability in the withdraw function that could allow a delegate to withdraw more ETH than they should be able to.
This calculates the amount to withdraw as the original delegated amount minus the active collateral. It then sets the delegate's delegated amount to just the active collateral.
The issue is that delegate.amount is not updated when collateral is marked as active. So if a delegate originally delegated 10 ETH, and currently has 9 ETH of that active, delegate.amount will still be 10 ETH.
Therefore, if they call withdraw:
• amountWithdrawn is calculated as 10 ETH (original amount) - 9 ETH (active collateral) = 1 ETH
• delegate.amount is then set to the active collateral of 9 ETH
This means the delegate has withdrawn 1 ETH, but their delegate.amount now shows 9 ETH, allowing them to withdraw another 1 ETH next time.


## Tools Used
Manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
delegate.amount should be updated whenever collateral is marked active


## Assessed type

Other

issues.title: `PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.deposit()` should call `perpetualAtlanticVault.updateFunding()` before calling `previewDeposit()`
Frontrunner can manipulate the delegate position struct between when it gets added and when the LogAddToDelegate event gets emitted.
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L961-L966


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The original user thinks they have a valid delegate position, when in fact the data belongs to the attacker. This could lead to loss of funds or manipulation of the system.

## Proof of Concept
There is a potential vulnerability here where a frontrunner could manipulate the delegate position struct between when it gets added and when the LogAddToDelegate event gets emitted.
The key issue is that the LogAddToDelegate event containing the delegate details is emitted after the delegate is added to the delegates array in the addToDelegate function. This creates a race condition where:
1. User calls addToDelegate to add a new delegate position.
2. delegates.push adds the new delegate to the array.
3. Before the event is emitted, a frontrunner calls withdraw to withdraw funds from the newly added delegate.
4. The original LogAddToDelegate event is emitted with details of the delegate position that no longer matches reality (as funds have now been withdrawn).
A proof of concept exploit would be:
A. Attacker watches for addToDelegate calls.
B. When addToDelegate is called, attacker frontruns and calls withdraw immediately, draining newly added delegate.
C. LogAddToDelegate event is emitted showing delegate details that are now inaccurate.
This could allow an attacker to game the system by withdrawing more funds than they are entitled to according to the delegate records.


## Tools Used
Manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps 
The contract should emit the event first before modifying state. It should emit the event before adding the delegate position


## Assessed type

Other

issues.title: PUT Option strike price can be much higher than 25% below the current price
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L270


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
If rDPX price is much lower than ETH price, PUT Option strike price can be much higher than 25% below the current price, this violates the invariant that PUT Option can only be created with strike price is 25% below the current price.

## Proof of Concept
As stated in the [code comment](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L270), PUT Option strike price should be 25% below the current price:
```
    uint256 strike = roundUp(currentPrice - (currentPrice / 4)); // 25% below the current price
```
The `currentPrice` is rDPX price in 8 dp denominated in ETH:
```
    uint256 currentPrice = getUnderlyingPrice(); // price of underlying wrt collateralToken
```
Currently, rDPX price is 20u and ETH price is 1700u, then the current price is 0.011e8 and PUT Option strike price should be 0.00825e8.
However, the strike price is [rounded up by roundUp method](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L576-L583):
```
  function roundUp(uint256 _strike) public view returns (uint256 strike) {
    uint256 remainder = _strike % roundingPrecision;
    if (remainder == 0) {
      return _strike;
    } else {
      return _strike - remainder + roundingPrecision;
    }
  }
```
=> remainder = _strike % roundingPrecision = 0.00825e8 % 1e6 = 0.00825e8 != 0
=> strike = _strike - remainder + roundingPrecision = 0.00825e8 - 0.00825e8 + 1e6 = 1e6
=> PUT Option strike price is much higher than 25% below the current price

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
It is recommended to set `roundingPrecision` to a much smaller value so that PUT Option strike price won't be rounded up to be much

issues.title: The price of DpxEth is not validated before performing debit/burn operations in the lowerDepeg function
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L1080-L1124


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
- Attacker manipulates price oracles to show DpxEth price below peg
- Attacker calls lowerDepeg, burning DpxEth tokens and draining ETH
- Attacker profits from improper burning/draining when price was actually still at peg


## Proof of Concept
There is a potential vulnerability if the price of DpxEth is not validated before performing debit/burn operations in the lowerDepeg function.
The lowerDepeg function is intended to be used when the price of DpxEth drops below the peg ratio of 1 DpxEth : 1 ETH. It allows burning DpxEth tokens and debiting ETH reserves to bring the ratio back to the peg.
However, there is no check of the current DpxEth price before performing these operations. This could allow an attacker to:
1. Manipulate the price oracles to show the DpxEth price is below the peg, even if it is not.
2. Call the lowerDepeg function to burn DpxEth tokens and debit ETH reserves.
3. This would inappropriately burn DpxEth tokens and drain ETH reserves even though the peg ratio is still intact.


## Tools Used
Manual
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
The lowerDepeg function should check the current DpxEth price from the oracles before performing any burn/debit operations. The price validation should happen right before the debits and burns occur


## Assessed type

Other

It assumes DpxEth will be sold, but doesn't enforce this. The newly minted DpxEth can be held instead, throwing off the peg.
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L1051-L1070


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The user could just mint DpxEth and hold onto it instead of selling it, which would not help bring the peg back down. User could mint a large amount of DpxEth without selling it, artificially inflating the DpxEth supply and potentially throwing off the peg.

## Proof of Concept
The way the upperDepeg function is currently implemented does not enforce that the newly minted DpxEth is actually sold. It mints new DpxEth to the contract and assumes it will be swapped for ETH. But it does not actually enforce the swap. 
This could potentially be exploited by:
1. User calls upperDepeg and mints a large amount of DpxEth
2. Instead of swapping the DpxEth for ETH, user transfers DpxEth to their own account
3. This increases DpxEth supply without decreasing the peg, defeating the purpose of upperDepeg 

Here are a few relevant points on this:
• The upperDepeg function allows an authorized caller (admin only) to mint new DpxEth by depositing ETH as collateral.
• There is no requirement enforced in the contract that the newly minted DpxEth must be sold right away. The key lines are: https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L1059-L1065
• By not enforcing the sale of DpxEth after minting, the caller could artificially inflate DpxEth supply without decreasing the peg price.
• Large amounts of undepegged DpxEth could significantly throw off the intended 1:1 peg to ETH.


In summary, the contract only checks that the price of DpxEth is above the upper peg, mints new DpxEth tokens, and swaps them for ETH. But it does not enforce that the received ETH is used to buy back and burn DpxEth to bring the price back down.


## Tools Used
Manual
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
- Require the newly minted DpxEth to be sold immediately

issues.title: Function `PerpetualAtlanticVault.purchase()` locks collateral but never send the collaterals to then LP vault
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L255-L312


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
One of the invariants of the protocol is that in order to lock the collateral, contract need to execute `PerpetualAtlanticVaultLp.lockCollateral()` to update the value of  `_activeCollateral` and then send the collateral to the LP vault, but the contract never send collaterals to the LP vault

This will make LP vault have the wrong `_activeCollateral` variable, causing wrong calculation later
## Proof of Concept
`PerpetualAtlanticVault.purchase()`:
```solidity
  function purchase(
    uint256 amount,
    address to
  )
    external
    nonReentrant
    onlyRole(RDPXV2CORE_ROLE)
    returns (uint256 premium, uint256 tokenId)
  {
    ...

    perpetualAtlanticVaultLp.lockCollateral(requiredCollateral);
    
    <@ NEVER send collateral to perpetualAtlanticVaultLp contract
    ...
  }
```
`PerpetualAtlanticVaultLp.lockCollateral()`:
```solidity
  function unlockLiquidity(uint256 amount) public onlyPerpVault {
    _activeCollateral -= amount;
  }
```
## Tools Used
Manual Review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Add this line to `PerpetualAtlanticVault.purchase()`:
```diff
   ...

   perpetualAtlanticVaultLp.lockCollateral(requiredCollateral);

+  collateralToken.safeTransferFrom(
      addresses.rdpxV2Core,
      addresses.perpetualAtlanticVaultLP,
      requiredCollateral
    );

   ...
```

# Lines of code

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Should update PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP collateral balance when settling an option or settle operation can be DOSed.

## Proof of Concept
[subtractLoss](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#L199) is called in [settle](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L315C12-L315C18) function to ensure enough collateral was sent out.
```
  function subtractLoss(uint256 loss) public onlyPerpVault {
    require(
      collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) == _totalCollateral - loss,
      "Not enough collateral was sent out"
    );
    _totalCollateral -= loss;
  }
```
The require statement in subtractLoss function requires that the collateral balance of the PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP should be strictly equal to (_totalCollateral - loss).
```
      collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) == _totalCollateral - loss
```
Please note ___totalCollateral__ is not updated when settling the option, an attacker can front-run and send 1 wei amount of collateral token to PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP, then the require statement will fail due to inequality.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
To mitigate this issue, please update PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP collateral balance when settling an option.

DoS

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Within the PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP#`redeem()`, there is no subtraction logic that the amount of WETH-transferred is subtracted from the `_totalCollateral` storage, which lead to misaccounting of the `_totalCollateral` storage that records the amount of WETH collateralized. 


## Proof of Concept

Within the PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP, the `_rdpxCollateral` would be defined to store the total amount of rDPX-collateralized like this:
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#L64
```solidity
  /// @dev Total rdpx available
  uint256 private _rdpxCollateral;  /// @audit
```

Within the PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP, the `_totalCollateral` would be defined to store the total amount of WETH-collateralized like this:
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#L58
```solidity
  /// @dev Total collateral available
  uint256 private _totalCollateral;   /// @audit
```

When a user would like to redeem the shares (VaultLP tokens) that the user hold, the user call the PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP#`redeem()`.
Within the PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP#`redeem()`, the following process would be proceeded like this:
- The amount of rDPX-withdrawn would be subtracted from the amount of rDPX-collateralized.
- Both underlying tokens ($WETH and $rDPX) would be transferred to the user (`receiver`) in exchange for burning the `shares` (VaultLP tokens) of the user (`receiver`).

issues.title: Denial of Service in Option Settlement
Potential Zeroing of reserveAsset Balance Due to Unadjusted totalWethDelegated on Withdrawal
Inaccurate Share Minting Due to Delayed Collateral Value Update in deposit Function
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#L118-L135


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `previewDeposit` function, which calculates shares based on assets and the current value of the collateral, can potentially mint more shares than appropriate. This is because the `updateFunding` function, which updates the `totalCollateral` value, is not called prior to `previewDeposit`. As a result, a new depositor could receive not only their rightful share but also an additional portion of the funds collected by other liquidity providers (LPs). This can lead to an unfair distribution of shares and potential financial loss for existing LPs.

## Proof of Concept
The `deposit` function calls `previewDeposit` to determine the number of shares to mint:
```javascript
function deposit(
    uint256 assets,
    address receiver
) public virtual returns (uint256 shares) {
    ...
    require((shares = previewDeposit(assets)) != 0, "ZERO_SHARES");
    ...
}
```
However, the `updateFunding` function, which adjusts the `totalCollateral` value, is called after `previewDeposit`:
```javascript
perpetualAtlanticVault.updateFunding();
```
This sequence of calls means that when `previewDeposit` calculates the shares, it does so based on an outdated value of the collateral. Consequently, depositors can receive an inflated number of shares.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Reorder the function calls in the deposit function to ensure that `updateFunding` is called before `previewDeposit`. This will ensure that shares are calculated based on the most recent collateral value.





## Assessed type

Math

# Lines of code

# Vulnerability details

## Summary
Attacker can deposit and redeem in same transaction to steal funding payment 
## Vulnerability Details
when a user deposits into PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP ,deposit function calculates amount of shares to be minted based on total supply and total collateral then calls perpetualAtlanticVault.updateFunding() to calculate and transfer pending funding to PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP , as new collateral has been added to vault value of shares increased and if user redeems it instantly he will get more than deposit amount , for example if user has deposited as much as 50% of vault collateral  he will get 50% of assest transferred via updateFunding so if he use flash loans he can take most of the fundings that has been paid to vault , this also can be used to take premium free options . 
## Impact
Attacker can steal funding payments made to PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP

## Proof of Concept
Let's say there is 1000 collateral in vault with total supply of 1000 .
1 - Alice takes a flashloan of 10000 collateral .
2 - Alice deposits 10000 collateral to vault ( 10000 shares calculated to mint for alice ) .
3 - deposit function calls updateFunding which transferes ( for example ) 100 collateral as funding and adds value to each vault share .
4 - 10000 shares has been minted for alice .
5 - Alice redeems all of her 10000 shares ans she'll receive nearly 10100 collateral instantly .

## Tools Used
Manual Review 
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Consider call perpetualAtlanticVault.updateFunding() before calculating shares .

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In the redeem function in the Perpetual Atlantic VaultLP contract, an attacker can easily redeem assets of a user or users.

## Proof of Concept
1. The Perpetual Atlantic VaultLP contract inherits the solmate ERC20 abstract contract and it implements an approve function which rerturns a boolean. 
2. This function is to be called by the owner who approves a certain spender in this case to redeem a certain amount of assets on their behalf. 
3. In a case where the user does not want a certain spender to spend (in this case redeem) a certain amount and want to decrease the spenders allowance lets say from 5 to 3, they can only call approve in the solmate token contract and set the new amount.
4. A malicious spender seeing the transaction an frontrun the user before they can set the new allowance.
5. A malicious spender can still redeem assets by frontrunning the user and redeeming the amount they were allowed to redeem prior(5) plus the new amount(3) just before the user sets a new allowance.
6. This can indeed cause huge loss for the user as the malicious spender can still redeem assets.

Manual review + h20

The present Perpetual Atlantic VaultLP contract inherits ERC20 from solmate. I would suggest to Inherit the ERC20 abstract contract from OpenZepellin instead of solmate so you can have access to decreaseallowance etc

If the function fails after the fund transfer but before the _updateFundingRate, the next call to this function will result in another fund transfer, which might not be the intended behavior.

## Proof of Concept
The function transfers funds using collateralToken.safeTransferFrom().
After transferring funds, let's say the function fails at _updateFundingRate(). This could happen for many reasons, like an out-of-gas error.
Given the function didn't complete its execution, a user or system might retry the function.
On the second execution, the function would again transfer funds, resulting in an unintended double transfer.

Manual Review

Introduce a state variable (a flag) to indicate if funding for a specific period (like the latestFundingPaymentPointer) has been processed. Before any state-changing actions, check this flag. If it indicates that funding was already processed, the function should exit early or revert.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The functions ``settle & payFunding`` are using the ``onlyRole(RDPXV2CORE_ROLE)`` modifier so that only the RdpxV2Core contract can use these functions but additionally they are also using the ``_isEligibleSender`` function that checks if a contract is whitelisted this is like having 2 sensitive roles for a contract which could lead to access control or Dos vulnerabilities in the contract.

## Proof of Concept
if these functions are meant to be used only by the **RdpxV2Core** contract, then it's not necessary to add the ``_isEligibleSender`` function because this requires adding the RdpxV2Core to the whitelisted contracts and if any other whitelisted contract (not the RdpxV2Core) is going to be used to call this functions then you should give this or these other contracts the ``RDPXV2CORE_ROLE`` and this could lead to vulnerabilities in the contract.

there's no problem adding the **RdpxV2Core** contract to the whitelisted contracts, but if you have a whitelisted contract that you want it to be able to use only these 2 functions(``settle & payFunding``) you will have to give the whitelisted contracts the ``RDPXV2CORE_ROLE`` and this will also give access to this contract to the whole RDPXV2CORE_ROLE functionality of the protocol, so if this contract is malicious or get compromised, the whole RDPXV2CORE_ROLE will get compromised too.

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L764
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L1051
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L1080


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

Due to a number of observed issues with the design and implementation of the Peg Stability Module (PSM), it cannot effectively restore the dpxETH-ETH peg in a depegging scenario.

## Proof-of-Concept

It is noted that the three core functions designed by the Project Team that compose the 'Peg Stability Module' are `settle`, `upperDepeg` and `lowerDepeg` all contained within the `RdpxV2.core.sol` contract. The Peg Stability Module is designed to restore the dpxETH-ETH peg in a depegging scenario.

Due to the attack shown previously (in report "Options can't be settled") where depositing 1 wei into the contract will make all admin calls to settle(...) revert, the intended functioning of the `settle` function as part of the Peg Stability Module to bring back the peg will be completely ineffective. 

For clarity, the PoC demonstrating that Atlantic Perpetual Put Options cannot be settled will be shown below:

**Atlantic Perpetual Put Options cannot be settled**

First an attacker sends 1 wei of collateral token to  `PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol`.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L598-L615


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The delegate and delegatee fee calculation involves rdpxRequiredInWeth directly and due to wrong precision it will lead to amount1 and amount2 calculated wrongly.

## Proof of Concept
In _calculateAmounts function in RdpxV2Core the rdpxRequiredInWeth is calculated by the equation:   
  uint256 rdpxRequiredInWeth = (_rdpxRequired * getRdpxPrice()) / 1e8
where _rdpxRequired should be translated in 1e8 precision and by dividing it by 1e8 it was intended to get the rdpxRequiredInWeth to 1e8 but _rdpxRequired is in 1e18 and dividing it by 1e8 makes it in 1e10 precision leaving it with extra 1e2 ( getRdpxPrice() will give the value in 1e8) and thus making the calculation wrong wherever it gets involved.
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L605C3-L605C73

It is directly involved in calculating amount1 and amount1 then further used to calculate amount2.
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L608-L614

This value will also be used in minting bond tokens 
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L736

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Consider dividing _rdpxrequired by 1e10
uint256 rdpxRequiredInWeth = (_rdpxRequired * getRdpxPrice()) / 1e10

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L465
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L603-L612


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
updateFundingPaymentPointer() is used as a Helper function that updates the latest funding payment pointer based on current timestamp.
updateFundingPaymentPointer() uses the currentFundingRate parameter:
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L465
uint256 currentFundingRate = fundingRates[latestFundingPaymentPointer];

## Proof of Concept
The fundingRates[latestFundingPaymentPointer] parameter is calculated in the _updateFundingRate() function:
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L603C7-L612
fundingRates[latestFundingPaymentPointer] =
     (amount * 1e18) /
     (endTime - startTime);
} else {
     uint256 startTime = lastUpdateTime;
     uint256 endTime = nextFundingPaymentTimestamp();
     if (endTime == startTime) return;
     fundingRates[latestFundingPaymentPointer] =
     fundingRates[latestFundingPaymentPointer] +
     ((amount * 1e18) / (endTime - startTime));
}

There may be situations when the latestFundingPaymentPointer has been updated, but the fundingRates[latestFundingPaymentPointer] parameter has still been calculated.

Calling the updateFundingPaymentPointer() function without calling _updateFundingRate() will result in updateFundingPaymentPointer() not functioning properly.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Add a call to _updateFundingRate() at the beginning of the updateFundingPaymentPointer() function

# Vulnerability details




## Impact
`RdpxV2Core.lowerDepeg()` and `RdpxV2Core.upperDepeg()` can be DoS'd by frontrunning with deposits/withdrawals/swaps on the Curve pools (and in the case of `lowerDepeg()` also the UniswapV2 pool) to cause an inequality constraint in `RdpxV2Core._curveSwap()` to be violated.

## Proof of Concept
[`RdpxV2Core.lowerDepeg()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L1080-L1124) burns dpxETH to restore the peg of dpxETH to wETH. It takes `_rdpxAmount` and `_wethAmount` from the reserves, swaps `_rdpxAmount` for `amountOfWethOut` on UniswapV2 and then swaps `_wethAmount + amountOfWethOut` for dpxETH on Curve, which is then burned.

The second swap is performed in `RdpxV2Core._curveSwap()` which [validates that `ethBalance + (_wethAmount + amountOfWethOut) <= (ethBalance + dpxEthBalance) / 2`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L534-L537), where `ethBalance` and `dpxEthBalance` are the balances in the Curve pool.

The vulnerability is that all of the terms, except `_wethAmount`, in the above inequality can be manipulated by an attacker such that the inequality is violated, causing `_curveSwap()` to revert and thus also `lowerDepeg()`.

The attacker may deposit wETH in the Curve pool to increase `ethBalance`, or withdraw dxpETH to decrease `dpxEthBalance`, or effectively do both at the same time by swapping wETH for dpxETH.
Or he may similarly manipulate the price in the UniswapV2 pool such that more `amountOfWethOut` is received than expected.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The contract RdpxV2Core.sol has functions to get price from oracle (https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L1206-L1242): getLpPrice() , getDpxEthPrice(), getEthPrice(), getRdpxPrice().

The getDpxEthPriceInEth() and getEthPriceInDpxEth() functions may return an incorrect price for an asset.

## Proof of Concept
After calling the getDpxEthPriceInEth() and getEthPriceInDpxEth() functions, they return the value of lastPrice or (DECIMALS * DECIMALS) / lastPrice respectively. However, this may not be the current price. Based on the functions, the price is correct if the following condition is met:

(https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/oracles/DpxEthOracle.sol#L107-L109, https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08 -dopex/blob/main/contracts/oracles/DpxEthOracle.sol#L118-L120)
if (block.timestamp > lastUpdated + heartbeat),
where lastUpdated = block.timestamp
heartbeat = 35 minutes

Thus, the price of an asset can be updated, for example, 30 minutes ago. This can lead to loss of assets when slipping in _curveSwap() due to incorrect price calculation.

For a more accurate price, you need to call the updatePrice() function (https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/oracles/DpxEthOracle.sol#L80-L99), which in turn must call the getDpxEthPriceInEth() and getEthPriceInDpxEth() functions to calculate the price.

Manual review

It is better to use the Chainlink service to get the price

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/reLP/ReLPContract.sol#L233


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

The formula to calculate `tokenAToRemove` amount in `ReLPContract.reLP` function is incorrect where the `tokenAInfo.tokenAReserve` is used instead of `rdpx_supply` or `IERC20(addresses.tokenA).totalSupply()` (check line 233) as specified in the [documentation](https://dopex.notion.site/rDPX-V2-RI-b45b5b402af54bcab758d62fb7c69cb4)

```solidity
// Findings are labeled with '<= FOUND'
// File: contracts/reLP/ReLPContract.sol
202:  function reLP(uint256 _amount) external onlyRole(RDPXV2CORE_ROLE) {
				...
232:    uint256 tokenAToRemove = ((((_amount * 4) * 1e18) /
233:      tokenAInfo.tokenAReserve) * // <= FOUND: should be rdpx_supply
234:      tokenAInfo.tokenALpReserve *
235:      baseReLpRatio) / (1e18 * DEFAULT_PRECISION * 1e2);
					...
307:  }
```

Since `tokenAInfo.tokenAReserve` is used, which is always much less than `rdpx_supply`, leading to the computed `tokenAToRemove` values that are much larger than expected. This can ultimately cause the whole bonding process to fail, even with a reasonable target amount of bond, due to the scaling factor of `rdpx_supply / tokenAReserve`. 

Additionally, if the `rdpxV2Core` contract enables the `isReLPActive` flag, this issue can make the bonding process inoperable if `rdpx_supply / tokenAReserve` is too large. Furthermore, a malicious attacker can use a reasonably smaller fund to force the removal of all liquidity provider (LP) tokens from the AMO, swap ETH to rDPX to pump the price, and simultaneously exploit the pump in the rDPX price with a flash MEV attack.

## Proof of Concept

1. Alice, who is aware of this vulnerability, interacts with the contract.
2. She performs actions that trigger the incorrect calculation of `tokenAToRemove` using `tokenAInfo.tokenAReserve`.
3. This leads to `tokenAToRemove` values that are much larger than expected, causing issues in the bonding

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Option writers can anticipate calls to PerpetualAtlanticVault.settle() to prevent any in-the-money option from being exercised, potentially allowing the backing of $dpxETH to fall down to its 75%ETH value under adverse market conditions.

## Proof of Concept
Whenever an option is settled, the Atlantic Vault will transfer collateral (that is, WETH) from the VaultLP contract to the Core contract to make up for the reduced rDPX value; subsequently, a call is made to the VaultLP to update its state, substracting the loss incurred from its _totalCollateral variable.

In the process however, a check is made that the current WETH balance of the contract *strictly* matches _totalCollateral minus the loss calculated by the Vault:
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#L199-L203

Hence sending 1 wei in advance is enough to trigger a revert of the settle() call.

The following addition to the existing *test-perp/Unit.testSettle()* unit test demonstrates how an otherwise successful call can be blocked :

issues.title: Precision loss due to incorrect calculation of bondDiscount.
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L1162-L1166


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
A use of the wrong denominator value when calculating `bondDiscount` leads to a precision of 1e10 instead of a precision of 1e8 as expected. As a result `bondDiscount` will be two orders or magnitude greater than its indended value, therefore leading to a loss of funds.


## Proof of Concept

Let's examine the `calculateBondCost` function. 

The `bondDiscount` is then used to calculate the amount of `weth` and `rdpx` required to initiate a bond under the condition [`_rdpxBondId is 0`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L1163-L1166)


```
  uint256 bondDiscount = (bondDiscountFactor *
        Math.sqrt(IRdpxReserve(addresses.rdpxReserve).rdpxReserve()) *
        1e2) / (Math.sqrt(1e18)); // 1e8 precision 

```

The value `bondDiscount` is intended to be to 1e8 precision. Since `IRdpxReserve(addresses.rdpxReserve).rdpxReserve()` returns 1e18 and the `bondDiscountFactor` as indicated by the development team, has a precision of 1e8. 



Lets breakdown the formula for calculating discount factor 

`bondDiscount * √IRdpxReserve(addresses.rdpxReserve).rdpxReserve() * 1e2 / √1e18`

Substituting for the expected precision values, we get:


```
1e8 * 1e9 * 1e2 / 1e9 =

1e19/1e9 =

1e10
```
 


## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

A simple solution to maintain 1e8 precision for the bondDiscount is to divide the numerator by `1e11` (or Math.sqrt(1e22) )

The code will need to be adjusted as follows:

```
 uint256 bondDiscount = (bondDiscountFactor *
        Math.sqrt(IRdpxReserve(addresses.rdpxReserve).rdpxReserve()) *
        1e2) / (Math.sqrt(1e22)); // 1e8 precision
```


## Assessed type

Decimal

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#L182


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
PerpetualAtlanticVault's settle function can always be reverted by an attacker.

If an attacker artificially transmits collateral tokens to PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP, the actual balance and _totalCollateral values are separated from the PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#substractLoss function and can always be reverted by the substractLoss function called from the PerpetualAtlanticVault#settle function.

## Proof of Concept
The PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#substractLoss function is as follows.
```
  function subtractLoss(uint256 loss) public onlyPerpVault {
    require(
      collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) == _totalCollateral - loss,
      "Not enough collateral was sent out"
    );
    _totalCollateral -= loss;
  }
```
Here, if you look at `collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) == _totalCollateral - loss`, it is assumed that collateral.balanceOf(this) and _totalCollateral values always match.
However, if an attacker transmits even a very small amount of collateral tokens (for example, 1), the collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) value increases and the _totalCollateral value does not increase.

At this time, IPerpetualAtlanticVaultLP(addresses.perpetualAtlanticVaultLP).subtractLoss called from the PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#settle function may result in always being reverted.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Instead of transferring the collateral token from PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP to transferFrom and calling substractLoss, an additional function must be implemented to perform both operations simultaneously.

Error

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L955
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L964


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The function addToDelegate allows users to delegate a certain amount of WETH.

It calculates a fee based on the _fee parameter and then creates a Delegate struct with the user's delegation details.

After creating the Delegate struct, it adds the _amount to the totalWethDelegated variable, which tracks the total amount of WETH delegated.

However, the order of operations here is crucial. If an attacker calls this function with a very large _amount (close to the maximum uint256 value), they can cause an integer overflow in the totalWethDelegated variable.

An integer overflow in totalWethDelegated could lead to incorrect accounting and allow attackers to exploit the system.

## Proof of Concept
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L955

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L964

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
To mitigate this risk, you should update the order of operations to first add the _amount to totalWethDelegated and then create the Delegate struct

totalWethDelegated += _amount;

Delegate memory delegatePosition = Delegate({
  amount: _amount,
  fee: _fee,
  owner: msg.sender,
  activeCollateral: 0
});
delegates.push(delegatePosition);

This change ensures that the total amount delegated is updated before creating the delegate position, preventing potential integer overflow vulnerabilities.



## Assessed type

Under/Overflow

Detailed description of the impact of this finding.

totalWethDelegated = newTotalWethDelegated;

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L181


# Vulnerability details

# Issue

The PerpetualAtlanticVault::setAddress() function is prone to frontrunning. Below is the core update that the PerpetualAtlanticVault::setAddress() function performs.
```
...
addresses = Addresses({
  optionPricing: _optionPricing,
  assetPriceOracle: _assetPriceOracle,
  volatilityOracle: _volatilityOracle,
  feeDistributor: _feeDistributor,
  rdpx: _rdpx,
  perpetualAtlanticVaultLP: _perpetualAtlanticVaultLP,
  rdpxV2Core: _rdpxV2Core
});
...
```

Link: [Code snippet](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L181)

This updates various addresses which are then used in other functions throughout the contract. If an admin updates the above addresses using the `PerpetualAtlanticVault::setAddress()` function, this can be frontrun and can lead to the usage of the old addresses.

# Impact
The most critical of all the above addresses is the `perpetualAtlanticVaultLP` address. Throughout the contract there are several uses of this address, including transfer of different tokens.
If the previous `perpetualAtlanticVaultLP` contract address is compromised, then the transaction to update the `perpetualAtlanticVaultLP` can be frontrun and transactions will be performed on the old compromised `perpetualAtlanticVaultLP` contract address.

# Tools Used
Manual analysis

# Recommended Mitigation Steps
If any addresses need to be updated in the contract, then the pause function should be utilised so any frontrunning attempts can be avoided.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L269-L273


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Immediate loss on vault liquidity provider side (Option Writers). All collateral in VaultLP could be drained within the same transaction if the protocol's offline algorithm detects the profits.

## Proof of Concept
The issue revolves around a lack of validation condition that allows immediate exercise of options when the market price falls below a certain threshold (`roundingPrecision`). This leads to a situation where the option can be exercised without any constraints, resulting in a positive profit for the option buyer, causing an immediate loss to the vault liquidity providers.

1. If the current market price (`currentPrice`) falls within the range `(0, roundingPrecision)`, Alice can buy an In-the-money option and can immediately exercise it at `strike` price of `roundingPrecision` which is 1e6 or 0.01weth thanks to `roundUp`. Alice can purchase an option with a strike price (`strike`) and an amount (`amount`) such that `strike * amount > premium`.
3. Alice exercises the option, receiving `strike * amount - premium` as profit.
4. As a result, the vault liquidity provider faces an immediate loss of collateral, as the option was exercised without any expiry constraints.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Do not allow option purchase if the market price falls below the `roundingPrecision`. FYI, setting `rdpxCoreV2.putOptionsRequired` flag to false is not sufficient since it can be front-run.


## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#L159


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Anyone can gain disproportionate amount of PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP shares instantly and can use them to drain almost all rDPX tokens from the contract.

The `deposit` function of PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP contract can be called by anyone. So anyone can deposit WETH and can collect vault shares. During redemption, the output WETH and rDPX amounts are calculated based upon the ratio of caller's shares balance and shares total supply.
```solidity
  function _convertToAssets(
    uint256 shares
  ) internal view virtual returns (uint256 assets, uint256 rdpxAmount) {
    uint256 supply = totalSupply;
    return
      (supply == 0)
        ? (shares, 0)
        : (
          shares.mulDivDown(totalCollateral(), supply),
          shares.mulDivDown(_rdpxCollateral, supply)
        );
  }
```
So anyone with huge shares balance can withdraw almost all rDPX tokens from the contract instantly.


## Proof of Concept
- The PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP contract contains 100 WETH and 1000 rDPX. Total supply of vault lp shares is 100e18.
- Attacker deposits 100,000 WETH to the vault and receives 100,000e18 vault shares.
- Attacker calls redeem and withdraws his 100,000 WETH and additional 999 rDPX tokens (100000 * 1000 / 100100).

A flash loan can be used to perform the above steps atomically and without any upfront capital. 

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Consider restricting the `deposit` function to Core contract only. Otherwise the economics of contracts will remain misaligned, in current state any depositor can withdraw more than the deposited amount instantly.


## Assessed type

Context

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#L201
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L359-L361


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

When some Put options can be settled, DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can settle these options by calling [RdpxV2Core.settle](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L764-L766). which will call internally [IPerpetualAtlanticVaultLP(addresses.perpetualAtlanticVaultLP).subtractLoss](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L359-L361) to [deduct the loss from _totalCollateral](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/main/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#L199-L204). But there is a check that `collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) == _totalCollateral - loss`, which can be broken. Malicious users can directly transfer a small amount of WETH to perpetualAtlanticVaultLP in advance to prevent `==` from being met. This leads to `settle` revert, which has the following impacts:

- No options can be settled. Core functionality is significantly broken.

# Vulnerability details

## Summary

The `PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP::subtractLoss()` function has a strict balance check with a `require`.

By providing any amount of collateral to it, like 1 wei, the function will always revert. This function is used by the `PerpetualAtlanticVault::settle()` function, which is called by the `RdpxV2Core::settle()` function.

This will make the settle function always revert.

## Impact

With a DOS of the `RdpxV2Core::settle()` function, no option can be settled. This can be undone as the strict balance check on the `substractLoss()` function will always make the function revert.

The attack is extremely cheap, and easy to exploit, just requiring the attacker to send 1 wei of collateral to the `PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP` contract at any time.

The root of the finding is this strict equality check.

Once an attacker sends any amount of collateral tokens to the contract, the `require` statement will not pass, making the function always revert.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

The function `subtractLoss` subtracts the loss amount from the vault's LP during a settlement. There is also a require statement which makes sure the balance in the contract lines up with the accounting.

```solidity
require(
      collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) == _totalCollateral - loss,
      "Not enough collateral was sent out"
    );
_totalCollateral -= loss;
```

The issue is that this condition can be easily violated with an external donation. The value in `_totalColalteral` is changed during deposits, redeems, premium additions, and losses. Importantly, it is NOT dependent on the actual contract balance. So even before loss reporting, the amount of collateral in the contract is not necessarily equal to `_totalCollateral`, since any user can send weth to the contract directly.

Lets assume the `_totalcollateral` is 100 WETH, and the actual balance is 101 WETH due to an external donation. During a `settle` call on the vault, WETH is withdrawn from the LP vault. Lets assume this amount is 50 WETH.

);

    ethAmount
);
```

After transferring WETH from ```PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP``` to the ```RdpxV2Core```, and RDPX is transferred from ```RdpxV2Core``` to the ```PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP```, ```PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.subtractLoss()``` is triggered to deduct the transferred WETH from ```_totalCollateral```.

```
require(
      collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) == _totalCollateral - loss,
      "Not enough collateral was sent out"
    );
```

## Tools Used
Manual review.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Consider changing the equality sign to less or equal.
```
require(
      collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) <= _totalCollateral - loss,
      "Not enough collateral was sent out"
    );
```

DoS

# Vulnerability details


`PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP` holders receives premium/funding for their deposited WETH, which are used to write `PerpetualAtlanticVault` put options.

However, they are able to redeem their WETH anytime as long as there are available WETH in `PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP`. As the losses from the options are deducted from `PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP` via `settle()`, `PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP` holders can evade the loss and redeem their WETH by frontrunning `settle()` operation. They can then backrun `settle()` to re-deposit the redeemed WETH at a lower share price.

Even though, Arbitrum does not have a mempool at the moment, there could possibly be MEV opportunities in the future when they decentralize the sequencer. And this issue is also applicable if the project intends to expand to other chains or make it omnichain.


## Impact
The issue can allow `PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP` holders to arbitrage by evading options while receiving premium/funding, causing the other holders to inccur higher losses.


## Proof of Concept
Imagine the following scenario,
1. Alice who is a `PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP` holder has deposited WETH in `PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP` and receives premium/funding for them.
2. Alice monitors for `settle()` transaction and proceed to frontrun them by calling `redeem()` to evade the option loss and withdraws her WETH & rDPX.
3. Alice can then backrun the `settle()` transactions with `deposit()`, to deposit the WETH & rDPX at a lower share price and continue to receive premium/funding for them.


## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Add in a time lock on `PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP` redemption, to allow holders to request redemption and only allow them to retrieve the WETH & rDPX after a certain period of time. 
Note that holders should not receive fundings upon redemption request.


## Assessed type

MEV

# Vulnerability details

A delegate bonding system is used by users who can delegate their WETH tokens, set a fee for the usage of these tokens, and other users holding rDPX can then bond using these pooled funds. The `withdraw` function allows a user who previously added WETH to the delegation pool via `addToDelegate` to withdraw any WETH that hasn't been actively used (bonded) by others.

However, when users retrieve their unused WETH from the delegate pool, the global state variable `totalWethDelegated` is not adjusted to reflect this withdrawal.

## Impact
Since the `totalWethDelegated` is not reduced when a delegate withdraws, the contract falsely believes there's more WETH available for delegation than there actually is. This can cause potential errors in subsequent bonding operations.

If the discrepancy between the contract's internal account (`totalWethDelegated`) and the actual amount of WETH delegated grows large, the `sync` function would always revert. This could happen if a malicious user repeatedly calls `addToDelegate` and `withdraw`, causing a potentially large value in `totalWethDelegated` to be subtracted from the actual balance. This subtraction might lead to a negative value, causing a revert and effectively disrupting reLP and AMO operations.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
At the start of every epoch the protocol admins will call `calculateFunding` in `PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol` to calculate the funding of options for an array of strikes prices in the next epoch. They do this before calling `provideFunding` in the core contract which calls the underlying `payFunding` in the vault contract. The provided funds are then dripped to the LPs throughout the epoch.

However a malicious user can frontrun the `provideFunding` transaction to purchase an option of a trivial amount (via creating a new bond) to cause the underlying `payFunding` call to fail. Based on the current logic there is no way to recover from this action because `calculateFunding` can't be called again, assuming the strike price of the option is the same as the strike price that funding has been calculated for. In the case where it is a new strike price, the attacker can simply do the same again after `calculateFunding` has been called to prevent funds from being provided to LPs for the epoch.

The end result is that a single user can prevent the vast majority of funds from being dripped to LPs, although the LPs will still receive some funding from options purchased during the epoch.

# Vulnerability details

## Summary

User can earn rDPX by repeatedly depositing and withdrawing because there are no rDPX tokens assigned to users.

## Vulnerability details

`PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP` contract does not implement any mechasim that assigns rDPX tokens to user's deposited collateral amount. When user wants to withdraw his tokens he calls `redeem` function which:
- transfers collateral back to user `collateral.transfer(receiver, assets)`
- transfers rDPX tokens to user as a reward `IERC20WithBurn(rdpx).safeTransfer(receiver, rdpxAmount)`
`rdpxAmount` is calculated in `redeemPreview` which calls internal function `_convertToAssets` 
```solidity

function _convertToAssets(
        uint256 shares
    ) internal view virtual returns (uint256 assets, uint256 rdpxAmount) {
        uint256 supply = totalSupply;
        return
            (supply == 0)
                ? (shares, 0)
                : (
                    shares.mulDivDown(totalCollateral(), supply),
                    shares.mulDivDown(_rdpxCollateral, supply)
                );
    }

```
`rdpxAmount` value is based on amount of `_rdpxCollateral` and `totalSupply` of shares.
This allows user to deposit and withdraw until there is enough `_rdpxCollateral` (rDPX tokens) in the contract.

## POC / Scenario 

1. Alice deposits 1000 collateral tokens, Bob deposits 1000 collateral tokens
2. They receive their amount of share based on the total supply of shares and total vault collateral (sum of collateral token and rdpx collateral multiplied by rpdx pirce in alpha token)
3. Alice decides to withdraw her 1000 collateral tokens using `redeem` function and receives her collateral back.

Any other user that will want to redeem his tokens and get collateral back will face a revert.

Manual review

Consider providing a timelock function or refactor the code to let users redeem a specific amount of rdpx tokens at single transaction.

```

This approach is problematic and introduces a security concern as it assumes a precise balance match, which can be disrupted by reentrancy or other concurrent operations.

The inconsistent balance check can lead to incorrect contract behavior and potentially unauthorized actions. }

The function assumes that the balance of the collateral token will be precisely equal to `_totalCollateral - loss` after the subtraction, which is not guaranteed due to potential reentrancy or other concurrent interactions.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The identified issue pertains to the potential occurrence of zero Ether payment during the bonding process, stemming from an error in the computation of the wrapped Ether (WETH) value within the ```RdpxV2Core.calculateBondCost()``` function. This issue would result in considerable losses for the protocol.

## Proof of Concept
The calculation of the rdpx and WETH values for a bond is facilitated by the RdpxV2Core.calculateBondCost() function. While calculating the rdpx value, the function multiplies RDPX_RATIO_PERCENTAGE with the _amount and DEFAULT_PRECISION (10^8), subsequently dividing the result by the rdpx price in Ether (ETH/WETH).

However, during the computation of the WETH value, although ETH_RATIO_PERCENTAGE is multiplied by the _amount, it is not multiplied by DEFAULT_PRECISION (10^8). This omission is grounded in the assumption that no division with a price is necessary due to the anticipated price of one for WETH/ETH. The core problem here is the oversight in accounting for rounding in the price, leading to a consistent rounding down against the protocol.

1. A user tries to bond an amount which is one.

```

# Lines of code

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The reentrancy vulnerability in the `bond` function could allow an attacker to `double-spend` the `rDPX` that they used to bond. This is because the function calls the `mintBond` function, which can be called by anyone. If an attacker calls the `bond` function and then immediately calls the `mintBond` function, they could potentially call the `mintBond` function `multiple times` before the first call has finished executing. This would allow them to mint `multiple bonds with the same rDPX`.

## Proof of Concept
- The attacker deposits `rDPX` into the contract.
- The attacker calls the `bond` function.
- The `bond` function calls the `mintBond` function.
- The attacker immediately calls the `mintBond` function again.
- The `mintBond` function mints a bond with the `rDPX` that the attacker deposited.
- The attacker repeats steps 4 and 5 until they have minted the desired number of bonds.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
- The `bond` function `should be modified` to use the modifier `nonReentrant` to prevent it from being called recursively.
- The `bond function `should be modified` to use the modifier `view` to prevent it from modifying any state.


## Assessed type

Reentrancy

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The reentrancy vulnerability in the `purchase` function could allow an attacker to `double-spend` the `premium`. This is because the function calls the `calculatePremium` function, which can be called by anyone. If an attacker calls the `purchase` function and then immediately calls the `calculatePremium` function, they could potentially call the `calculatePremium` function multiple times before the first call has finished executing. This would allow them to `double-spend` the `premium`.

## Proof of Concept
- The attacker calls the `purchase` function with a large amount of premium.
- The attacker immediately calls the `calculatePremium` function.
- The `calculatePremium` function calculates the `premium` for the purchase.
- The `purchase` function transfers the `premium` to the attacker.
- The attacker `cancels` the purchase.
The attacker is now able to keep the `premium` that they paid for the purchase.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
- The `purchase` function should be modified to use the `require` statement to check that the `calculatePremium` function has not been called before.
- The `calculatePremium` function should be modified to use the modifier `nonReentrant` to prevent it from being called recursively.
- The `calculatePremium` function should be modified to use the modifier view to prevent it from modifying any state.

Reentrancy

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
This vulnerability `allows an attacker to mint an infinite number of LP tokens` by passing in a value for assets that is too large. This could be exploited to cause a `denial-of-service` attack on the contract or to inflate the value of the `LP` tokens.

- The attacker creates a new contract that inherits from `PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol`.

- The `attacker can then withdraw` these `LP` tokens and sell them on the market, c`ausing the price of the LP tokens to inflate`.

Manual review

- Use a safe math library to prevent integer overflow errors. For example, the contract could use the `SafeMath` library from OpenZeppelin.
- Validate the input parameters to the `convertToShares` function to make sure that they are within a safe range.
- Use a `unit testing framework` to test the `convertToShares` function for overflow errors.

DoS

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/core/RdpxV2Core.sol#L975-L991


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
When a user delegates WETH by calling the ``addToDelegate()`` function, the state variable ``totalWethDelegated`` is increased in the following way:
```totalWethDelegated += _amount;``` 
But this variable isn't subtracted when the same user withdraws unused delegated WETH through the ``withdraw()`` function.
This implies that the user has the ability to delegate a substantial quantity of WETH (updating "totalWethDelegated" with that specific amount), and subsequently withdraw that amount without causing any impact on the value of ``totalWethDelegated``.

The area of main concern regarding this problem is the ``sync()`` function in ``RdpxV2Core`` contract. This function is supposed to "sync asset reserves with contract balances" and uses the ``totalWethDelegated``state variable by subtracting it to the balance of the ``reserveAsset`` (in the case of it being WETH):

``` 
if (weth == reserveAsset[i].tokenAddress) {
   balance = balance - totalWethDelegated;
} 
```

A malicious user can easily make ``sync()`` underflow. He simply has to increase the ``totalWethDelegated`` to a value superior to the contract's WETH balance.

Every function that calls the ``sync()`` function becomes unusable, namely:
* ``UniV3LiquidityAMO._sendTokensToRdpxV2Core()``
* ``ReLPContract.reLP()``

From here the effects of this bug start to spread, due to the importance of the functions affected.

In the case of ``UniV3LiquidityAMO._sendTokensToRdpxV2Core()``, the following functions become unavailable:
* ``UniV3LiquidityAMO.addLiquidity()``
* ``UniV3LiquidityAMO.removeLiquidity()``
* ``UniV3LiquidityAMO.swap()``

We should pay special attention to ``UniV3LiquidityAMO.removeLiquidity()`` because it prevents the protocol from removing liquidity, locking all liquidity provided to Uniswap V3.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVault.sol#L286-L286

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/libraries/BlackScholes.sol#L28


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Detailed description of the impact of this finding.

BlackScholes.calculate() used by optionPricingSimple.getOptionPrice() to calculate optionPrice in PerpetualAtlanticVault.calculatePremium() expects `timeToExpiry` to be in days but it's in block.timestamp which is timestamp of the current block in seconds since the epoch

This will result in wrong calculation of `put Time Decay` in BlackScholes.calculate() which will affect the optionsPrice. see here -- https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/libraries/BlackScholes.sol#L28, https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/libraries/BlackScholes.sol#L84

This will affect the calculation for premium in PerpetualAtlanticVault.purchase().

# Lines of code

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The reentrancy vulnerability in the `redeem` function allows an attacker to withdraw their `LP` tokens twice. This is because the function does not check if the first transaction has been mined before calling the function again.

This vulnerability could be exploited by an attacker as follows:

- The attacker calls the redeem function, withdrawing their `LP` tokens.
- The attacker then calls the redeem function again before the first transaction has been mined.
- The second transaction will also withdraw the attacker's `LP` tokens, resulting in a double withdrawal.

This vulnerability could result in a loss of funds for the contract.

## Proof of Concept
The proof of concept for the reentrancy vulnerability is as follows:

- The attacker creates a contract with a function that calls the `redeem` function.
- The attacker deposits `LP` tokens into the contract.
- The attacker calls the function in the contract, withdrawing their `LP` tokens.
- The attacker then calls the `redeem` function again before the first transaction has been mined.
- The second transaction will also withdraw the attacker's `LP` tokens, resulting in a double withdrawal.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
The following mitigation steps can be taken to fix the reentrancy vulnerability:

- The `redeem` function could be made non-reentrant. This can be done by using a mutex or a lock to prevent the function from being called recursively.
- The `redeem` function could be modified to check if the first transaction has been mined before calling the function again.


## Assessed type

Reentrancy

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/amo/UniV3LiquidityAmo.sol#L290

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Several contracts in the codebase utilize the transfer method for token transfers. The transfer method does not provide feedback on its success or failure, which can lead to unexpected contract behavior. If a transfer fails but the contract continues its execution, it can result in inconsistencies, such as minting shares without successfully transferring tokens.

## Proof of Concept
General Issue:
Many contracts, such as UniV3LiquidityAmo.sol, use the transfer method which lacks error handling.

Detailed Example:
In the PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol contract, the following sequence of operations is observed:
```
underlying.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);
_mint(msg.sender, shares);

```
If the transferFrom method fails for any reason (e.g., insufficient allowance, token contract issues), the contract will still proceed to mint shares, leading to a discrepancy between the actual assets held by the contract and the minted shares.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
- Replace all instances of transfer and transferFrom with their "safe" counterparts, safeTransfer and safeTransferFrom, which revert the transaction with an error message if the transfer fails.
- For critical operations, such as minting shares in the PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP contract, ensure that token transfers are successful before proceeding with further logic.


## Assessed type

Token-Transfer

# Vulnerability details

The removeAllLiquidityAndCollect function in the UniV3LiquidityAmo contract iterates over the positions_array, which can lead to a potential denial of service (DoS) attack if the array becomes too lengthy. In the provided code section, the function iterates over the positions_array:
```
for (uint i = 0; i < positions_array.length; i++) {
    // ... logic for removing liquidity and collecting tokens ...
}

```
If the positions_array grows too large, the loop's execution could consume more gas than the block gas limit, causing the function to fail.

## Tools Used
Manul review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
- Consider passing the positions array as a parameter to the removeAllLiquidityAndCollect function, allowing the caller to specify which positions to process. This approach provides flexibility in processing a subset of positions if needed.
- Implement pagination or batch processing for the removal of liquidity, allowing the operation to be split across multiple transactions.
- Add checks or limits on the size of the positions_array to prevent it from growing excessively large.

DoS

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Attacker can DoS settle() function's execution, lead to loss of fund

## Proof of Concept
When admin call RDPXV2Core#settle() , it will make a call to PerpetualAtlanticVault#settle():

        (amountOfWeth, rdpxAmount) = IPerpetualAtlanticVault(
            addresses.perpetualAtlanticVault
        ).settle(optionIds);
In PerpetualAtlanticVault#settle(), there is a call to PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP#subtractLoss():

        IPerpetualAtlanticVaultLP(addresses.perpetualAtlanticVaultLP)
            .subtractLoss(ethAmount);
Problem raised in require condition in PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP#subtractLoss():

    function subtractLoss(uint256 loss) public onlyPerpVault {
        require(
            collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) == _totalCollateral - loss, //<------------
            "Not enough collateral was sent out"
        );
        _totalCollateral -= loss;
    }
In PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP, _totalCollateral does not accurately reflect amount of collateral in contract. Attacker simply just need to directly deposit any token to PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP but not in deposit() function, this condition will be break, which make function being reverted.

## Tools Used
Manual review.

It is really hard to fix this issue, other mechanism should be implemented to mitigrate this problem

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In the RdpxV2Core contract's constructor, a "Zero" asset is added to the reserveAsset array, but there is no corresponding addition to the reserveTokens array. Both these arrays are used the same way in the functions  addAssetTotokenReserves and removeAssetFromtokenReserves, implying they should maintain a consistent state. However, due to this inconsistency, when an asset is removed, the reserveTokens array ends up removing an unintended asset. Consequently the reserveIndex is updated with the reserveTokens breaking its accounting too.

Consequences:
 
1. **`reserveIndex`** faulty accounting will compromise the functionality of methods like:
    - _purchaseOptions, _stake, _transfer, _bondWithDelegate, provideFunding, bond, upperDepeg, lowerDepeg, getReserveTokenInfo.
3. Protocol unable to remove/add more tokens to avoid breaking accounting further.
2. Misleading information presented on the frontend. 

## Proof of Concept
Lets simulate a scenario to show the effects

Starting balances 

**reserve tokens** RDPX, WETH, DPXETH
**reserve index** RDPX → 1, WETH → 2, DPXETH → 3
**reserve assets** ZERO, RDPX, WETH, DPXETH

Remove WETH from token reserves

**reserve tokens after WETH removal** RDPX, WETH
**reserve index after WETH removal** RDPX → 1, WETH → 0, DPXETH → 2
**reserve assets after WETH removal** ZERO, RDPX, DPXETH

Remove DPXETH from token reserves

**reserve tokens after DPXETH removal** RDPX
**reserve index after DPXETH removal** RDPX → 1, WETH → 2, DPXETH → 0
**reserve assets after DPXETH removal** ZERO, RDPX

**Foundry test case**

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP contract is vulnerable to flash loan attacks. A malicious actor can exploit the distribution mechanism by performing a rapid deposit-withdrawal sequence, allowing them to benefit disproportionately from accumulated collateral.

The root of the problem lies in the different timings of the **`updateFunding()`** function call between deposit and withdrawal functions. During a deposit, the shares are calculated before the **`updateFunding()`** call. In contrast, during withdrawal, assets are calculated after **`updateFunding()`** is invoked. This inconsistency, combined with the potential for accumulated tokens if **`updateFunding()`** hasn't been called for a significant period, creates an exploitable scenario.

Scenario

1. The attacker takes a large flash loan.
2. They deposit it into the contract. The shares they receive are based on the contract's current accounting without the latest funding.
3. Immediately after, the attacker triggers a withdrawal. The withdrawal first calls **`updateFunding()`**, adding funding.
4. The attacker then redeems their shares, which are now worth more due to the recent update from **`updateFunding()`**.

## Proof of Concept
### **1. Initial state:**

- **`totalSupply`** of shares: 100
- **`_totalCollateral`**: 1,000
- **`_rdpxCollateral`** and its conversion rate: 10 (with a conversion rate of 10)

### **2. A user takes a flash loan of 500**

### **3. Deposit 500:**

When depositing, the formula used is:

- **`totalVaultCollateral`** = totalCollateral() + ((_rdpxCollateral * rdpxPriceInAlphaToken) / 1e8);
- **`shares`** = assets.mulDivDown(supply, totalVaultCollateral)

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Detailed description of the impact of this finding.
DOS attack can be launched to  PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.subtractLoss(). This is because the condition `` collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) == _totalCollateral - loss`` will always fail if a malicious user donates some collateral tokens to the PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP contract. 


## Proof of Concept
Provide direct links to all referenced code in GitHub. Add screenshots, logs, or any other relevant proof that illustrates the concept.

``PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.subtractLoss()`` allows the ``PerpetualAtlanticVault`` contract to readjust the value of ``_totalCollateral`` based on the input ``loss``. It checks that `` collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) == _totalCollateral - loss``

[https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#L199-L205](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-dopex/blob/eb4d4a201b3a75dd4bddc74a34e9c42c71d0d12f/contracts/perp-vault/PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.sol#L199-L205)]

However, if a malicious user donates some collateral tokens to the PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP contract, then the condition ``collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) == _totalCollateral - loss`` will break forever, and therefore, subtractLoss() will be blocked forever. 

Therefore, a user can easily launch a DOS attack to  PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.subtractLoss() and PerpetualAtlanticVault.settle() (since it calls the former) by sending free collateral tokens to the PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP contract.

## Tools Used
VSCode

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Change the condition ``collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) == _totalCollateral - loss`` to `` collateral.balanceOf(address(this)) >= _totalCollateral - loss`` to prevent donation-based DOS attack:
